items.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So I hired Alex, and we had a band and we started rehearsing... So the band was called Directions... Well, Mike left and Alex left.

ctx.x: Even though you had a four record deal?

Yeah. We did one more record, and actually there was an instrumental that I wrote called “Festival” that CBS wanted to push as a single, but again we had no money to go out and tour. So at that point I said “Okay I’m gonna go sink or swim with jazz.” They let us out of the contract, and I went back to deciding to be a bandleader and I think

my first band had John Abercrombie… I had been working with a group with John and Mick Goodrick; master guitarist and educator who teaches at Berklee. I had the two guitars and a bassist named Clint Houston. So I called on John. John had been working with Chico Hamilton, and so John played spacy guitar and could go a lot of places I wanted to go. (He) had a sense of humor. So, I think that first bass player was named Peter Warren at the time. I was looking for a saxophone player and I think that Alex Foster was…
